title: Etale base neighbourhood making a prescribed nodal fibre point rational and split
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to S_0$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where $X_0,S_0$ are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and at every nonsmooth point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] its maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is isomorphic as an $\Omega$-algebra to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Fix $x_0\in X_0$ where $f_0$ is not smooth, and put $s_0=f_0(x_0)$ and $k=\kappa(s_0)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there exist an affine scheme $V_1$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, an etale morphism $e:(V_1,v_1)\to(S_0,s_0)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and a point $x_1\in X_1=X_0\times_{S_0}V_1$ [def-pc-fibre-product] projecting to $x_0$ and $v_1$, such that the induced field extension $K=\kappa(v_1)$ over $k$ is finite separable [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], the base-changed morphism $f_1:X_1\to V_1$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, the induced map $K\to\kappa(x_1)$ is an isomorphism, and
$$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{(X_1)_{v_1},x_1}\cong K[[u,v]]/(uv)$$
as $K$-algebras. Here $(X_1)_{v_1}$ denotes the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and the hat denotes completion at the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Put $C=(X_0)_{s_0}$ and let $z\in C$ be the point over $x_0$, using the homeomorphism in [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Finite presentation implies finite type: by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], for all affine opens $U\subseteq X_0$, $V\subseteq S_0$ with $f_0(U)\subseteq V$ the ring map $\mathcal O_{S_0}(V)\to\mathcal O_{X_0}(U)$ is of finite presentation, so the displayed finite list of variables generates $\mathcal O_{X_0}(U)$ as an algebra; hence $f_0$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], and the quasi-compactness hypothesis is already given [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $C$ is finite type over $k$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2). The iterated base-change identification [def-pc-base-change] identifies $C_\Omega$ with the given geometric fibre for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, so $C$ satisfies the geometric hypotheses of [lem-trf-nodal-point-finite-separable-splitting]. Moreover $z$ is nonsmooth: $x_0$ belongs to $\operatorname{Sing}(f_0)$, whose formation and nonsmooth underlying set commute with base change by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular]; applying its last clause to $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S_0$ puts $z$ in the nonsmooth locus of $C/k$.

source.place: Tags 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family), 0C5B (lemma-base-change-nodal-family), and 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), first proof, residue-field paragraph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-point-finite-separable-splitting] to $C/k$ and $z$. It supplies a finite separable extension $L/k$ and an $L$-rational point $z_L\in C_L$ above $z$, together with an $L$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_L,z_L}\cong L[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-neighbourhood-prescribed-residue-field] to $S_0,s_0,L/k$. Obtain an etale $U\to S_0$, a point $v\in U$ over $s_0$, and a field isomorphism $\alpha:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa_U(v)$ compatible with the structural maps from $k$.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family), first proof, second paragraph; Tags 0CBT/0CBU/0CBW and More on Morphisms Tag 02LF (lemma-realize-prescribed-residue-field-extension-etale).

proof.text: Choose the affine neighbourhoods $V_1=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U$ of $v$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S_0$ of $s_0$ provided by local finite presentation of $U\to S_0$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; thus $V_1$ maps into $W$ and $A$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra. The restriction $e:V_1\to S_0$ is etale by [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction], taking the target open to be all of $S_0$. Since $S_0\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] says $R$ is generated over $\mathbf Z$ by finitely many elements $r_i$. If $a_j$ generate $A$ over $R$, the images of $r_i$ together with the $a_j$ generate $A$ over $\mathbf Z$: expand each polynomial in the $a_j$ and then its coefficients in the $r_i$. Thus the affine $V_1$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$. Write $v_1=v$ in this open subscheme and $K=\kappa_{V_1}(v_1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], restriction gives a residue-field isomorphism $\kappa_U(v)\to K$; compose it with $\alpha$ and again call the resulting $k$-isomorphism $\alpha:L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Hence $K/k$ is finite separable: transport a finite basis through $\alpha$, and transport separable annihilating polynomials through the equality of its $k$-structures.

Form $X_1=X_0\times_{S_0}V_1$. Its projection $f_1$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The cartesian fibre identification of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] gives $(X_1)_{v_1}\cong C_K$ over $K$, compatibly with the maps to $X_0$. Regard $C_L$ as a $K$-scheme using $\alpha^{-1}:K\to L$. The scalar-change isomorphism $C_L\cong C_K$ is, on each affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset C$, induced by $B\otimes_k L\to B\otimes_k K$, $b\otimes\lambda\mapsto b\otimes\alpha(\lambda)$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Its inverse uses $\alpha^{-1}$; the formulas commute with restriction, hence glue. Let $z_K$ be the image of $z_L$. Its residue field is $K$, with its structural identification transported by $\alpha$. The induced local-ring isomorphism identifies maximal ideals and all their powers, hence their inverse-limit completions. Apply $\alpha$ coefficientwise to $L[[u,v]]/(uv)$; this respects every truncation and fixes the relation $uv$, giving the $K$-algebra isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_K,z_K}\cong K[[u,v]]/(uv)$.

proof.text: Let $x_1$ be the image in $X_1$ of the point of $(X_1)_{v_1}$ corresponding to $z_K$. The fibre-product projections give $f_1(x_1)=v_1$ and image $x_0$ in $X_0$, since $z_L$ lay over $z$. To verify the residue-field clause in the total space, choose affine charts around $x_1,v_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] their fibre has coordinate ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(v_1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-residue-field-iso] the local map from the total-space local ring to the fibre local ring induces an isomorphism $\kappa_{X_1}(x_1)\to\kappa_{(X_1)_{v_1}}(z_K)$. Its composite with the structural map $K\to\kappa_{X_1}(x_1)$ is the already bijective structural map of $z_K$. Therefore $K\to\kappa_{X_1}(x_1)$ is an isomorphism. The fibre isomorphism in step 4 identifies $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{(X_1)_{v_1},x_1}$ with $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C_K,z_K}$ as $K$-algebras, so step 4 supplies exactly the requested split equation. This completes all clauses.
